recommendations.thesis: This is an update to the TLT long opened 2026-11-04 at 80.30, now 82.24 (+2.4%); the decision is hold with the hard stop unchanged and a trailing plan added. The original thesis was duration into a slowing economy; what has happened is better than that. With a December hike ~92% priced — re-verified live this morning off Kalshi's own API, KXFEDDECISION-26DEC-H25 at 92c bid / 93c ask on 3,061,423 contracts of open interest against 0-1c for any cut — the long end is trading as a bull flattener rather than a bear steepener: 10y-2y compressed from +0.28 to +0.24 in a single session while TLT made a higher high, which is the tape saying a credible inflation-fighting Fed caps the long end rather than lifting it. RED TEAM CORRECTION: the published thesis closed by saying that from 82.24 'the remaining distribution is better than it was at entry'. It is materially worse, and the sign is the wrong way round. The target is +2.06 away and the stop -3.44, a forward 0.60:1 against the 2.67:1 the trade was taken at. 48.5% of the move to target has been captured while the stop has not moved — the identical situation HII's update identifies and manages, so TLT now gets the identical treatment instead of a different one.
recommendations.key_risk: The 10-year real yield near 2.88% is at cycle highs and a hawkish dot plot or a 50bp surprise on Dec 9 re-steepens the curve and takes TLT through 79 in days. A secondary risk is that the stop at 78.80 sits 1.88 ATR from entry against an 1.8 ATR ETF floor — it clears, but barely, so a modest rise in realised vol would make this a stop too tight to publish fresh.
recommendations.counter_argument: If inflation is genuinely re-accelerating — core PCE +3.8% y/y in October, and the Fed minutes record participants open to more than 25bp — then the long end should demand more term premium, not less, and every duration long in 2026 has been wrong. The answer is that this is why the position is held rather than added to, and why it has a time stop: the bull-flattener claim is falsifiable by Dec 19. ON THE WIN PROBABILITY, which research left underived: 0.46 against the 0.272 entry-based baseline is an 18.8-point claim, and the derivation is the one HII uses. From the current 82.24 a driftless walk touches 84.30 before 78.80 with probability 3.44/(2.06+3.44) = 62.5%, so 0.46 is conservative against where the position actually stands and is a large claim only against a baseline computed from a 2026-11-04 entry. CONVICTION CUT 4 to 3: the three evidence kinds are real and the Kalshi quotes, open interest, contract close time and both moving averages all verified first-hand, but the technical leg was overstated, and research itself recorded that it would not open this position fresh at a 1.88 ATR stop. A 4 gets sized larger than that deserves.

watchlist.instrument: Kalshi: will core CPI rise more than 0.2% in November 2026? (resolves on single-decimal SA BLS core m/m; YES needs a printed 0.3%)
watchlist.note: The only real event-contract candidate found, and deliberately not taken. Quotes yes 45/46c, no 54/55c, OI 34,680 but only 200 contracts of 24h volume; closes 2026-12-10 08:25 ET, can_close_early true. The Cleveland Fed nowcast (updated 11/25) is +0.21% core m/m against a fetched FRED CPILFESL run of +0.22, +0.29, +0.33, +0.30 — three straight prints that would each have resolved YES. A printed 0.3 needs an unrounded >=0.25, i.e. +0.04pp above the nowcast, which at a nowcast sigma of 0.09-0.13pp is P(YES) ~33-38% against the market's 45-46%, so NO at 55c looks like a 9-point edge worth +16% over 14 days. It is not an edge: backing out the full ladder gives P(<=0.1) 12.5%, P(0.2) 42%, P(0.3) 35.5%, P(>=0.4) 9.5%, a mean of ~0.24% — almost exactly halfway between the nowcast's 0.21 and the 0.30 three-month run rate. The market is explicitly splitting the model against the momentum, and buying NO is a wholesale bet on the model with core accelerating and tariff passthrough still arriving.
watchlist.trigger: Buy NO only if the Cleveland Fed core-CPI nowcast drifts to 0.18% or below while this contract still bids 45c or better — a real disagreement rather than a coin flip.
